new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Opened (28-page chapter extract of PL 529; footer on each page: 'Online edition licensed 2015 CC BY-SA 4.0.. DOI:10.15144/PL-529.1'). Rendered PDF p. 2 (= chapter p. 2, section '2 Explanatory notes on Salako phonemics and morphophonemics', subsection 'Phonemes') to PNG and read it against the text layer. The passage is there. The stress sentence is exactly verbatim: 'Stress is non-phonemic and falls on the last syllable.' The only difference is in the vowel list of the reader's quote: the printed page reads 'i, e, ə, a, o, õ, u and ũ' (nasal õ, consistent with the next paragraph 'only õ and ũ are phonemic'), whereas the reader's quote has 'o, ɔ, u and ũ' (ɔ for õ); this is a transcription s…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress is not contrastive and falls on the final syllable of the word. Corroborated in the same paper by the transcription of the ethnonym Kendayan as [kanay'otn] ~ [kanay'ɔtn] (fn. 4, p. 1), with the stress mark before the last syllable.
new_statements.exceptions: None mentioned. Note the older conflicting report: Dunselman 1949 (BKI 105: 61) says the Mempawah-hinterland Kendayan (Ahe-area) dialect 'has a clear accent on the penultimate' ('een duidelijk accent op de paenultima'), with no schwa in the language. Whether this is a real Salako-vs-Ahe dialect difference or a missionary's Malay-coloured impression is not resolved by any opened source.
new_statements.domain_note: One-sentence phonemic note in a morphology paper, based on the author's 1986-1990 fieldwork on Salako (bahasa Damea) of Sambas regency / Lundu, main informant from Nyarumkop; word level; no phrase-level or citation-form discussion. The paper defers to Adelaar 1991 (VICAL 2) for the full phonology; Adelaar 2005 (Harrassowitz sketch grammar) presumably restates it.
new_statements.identity_note: The quoted statement is for Salako (bahasa Damea/Badamea), the Kendayan/Kanayatn dialect of Sambas regency (West Kalimantan) and Lundu (Sarawak); Glottolog treats Salako (retired ISO [skl], bookkeeping languoid sela1262) as part of the language-level kend1254 (ISO [knx] since the 2008 merge, CR 2007-261), and Adelaar 2002 p. 1 says Salako 'is mutually intelligible with Ahe, Belangin and some other dialects with which it forms the Kendayan dialect chain'. The older Dunselman 1949 remark (penultimate accent) is for the Mempawah-hinterland Kendayan of the Ahe area (Glottolog bookkeeping ahea1240; file also held). The two statements disagree (final vs penultimate); file under kend1254 with dialect = Salako, and flag the Ahe/Kendayan-proper stress placement as unresolved pending Lansau 1981 or Adelaar 2005.

readall_conflicts: The single listed work (Lansau et al. 1981) could not be read past its front matter, so it adds neither agreement nor disagreement. 2, 'Stress is non-phonemic and falls on the last syllable' (Salako/Badamea, final) versus Dunselman 1949, BKI 105, p. 61, 'heeft daarbij een duidelijk accent op de paenultima' (Kendayan of the Mempawah hinterland, Ahe area, penultimate). These describe different dialects of the Kendayan cluster and differ in rigour (a phonemic note by a linguist vs. a missionary's introductory remark), so the catalog's fixed: final syllable record for Salako stands, with the Dunselman penult statement flagged as a dialect-level disagreement, not a refutation.
